outlineStatus: Provisional broad lowland envelope interpreted from the author’s 1805 marsh map, book and registered 1848–51 regional atlas. Not a surveyed marsh boundary or hydraulic boundary. Local ground evidence takes precedence.

interpolation.method: inverse distance weighting of all accepted early proxies with smooth Gaussian distance taper
interpolation.outsidePointHull: estimated continuation, explicitly not measured support

policy: Underlying marsh is a regional early-evidence surface across the whole lowland envelope, including later developed plots. Modern fill never supplies its interior baseline. Add later roads, yards, railways and bank/wall surfaces only within their own mapped footprints and evidence reach.
regionalInterpretation: Northern Hackney/Temple 14–15 ft; Stratford about 11–13 ft, with lower eastern-lane observations; northern Mill Meads about 8 ft; Abbey/Plaistow marsh generally 4–6 ft. Each estimate is representative rather than an exact floor reading.
limitations: Envelope edges are approximate. The transition is a modelling blend into adjoining non-marsh terrain, not a natural escarpment.
Southern Mill Meads has sparse early interior evidence; compare its later reviewed 7.3/7.7 ft ground readings before inferring a uniform southward drop.
River crossing by regional interpolation expresses a broad substrate trend, not flood connectivity. Surface-specific corrections remain confined to dry land.
Factory sites without usable yard readings retain an explicitly uncertain substrate estimate; a building footprint alone does not establish fill height.
laterGroundPolicy: Only accepted observations explicitly classified marsh, or independently reviewed ground, constrain the substrate. Unreviewed open-ground/premises and embankment-foot levels remain separate surface evidence. Corrections from the modern-derived outer model cannot propagate into the fully early-evidence interior.
